correctness.rationale: All stated labelled state counts, edge counts, component orders, component radii/diameters, eccentricities and all 36 positive-distance histogram coefficients were reproduced independently, without executing the deposited checker. All assignments in the named palette are candidates, including those that leave a colour unused. The cube symmetries and palette permutations preserve shortest paths; taking one full-graph BFS per genuine symmetry orbit and weighting by its cardinality counts each ordered pair once, and dividing by two then counts unordered pairs at positive distance. In particular the three concluding bins were 279, 15198 and 85870, and every nonisolated state had eccentricity 12. The four-colour isolation assertion also follows without computation: a proper colouring is frozen iff each vertex has three differently coloured neighbours, i.e. all vertices at distances one and two have distinct colours. This is equivalent to rainbow squares. The colour classes must then be the four antipodal pairs, giving 4! = 24 colourings in one colour-renaming orbit. At k=2 the connected bipartite cube gives two isolated assignments. This is exhaustive only for the stated finite domain and is not formal verification.

evidence: Feghali–Johnson–Paulusma prove that for connected graphs of maximum degree at least three, any two nonfrozen (Delta+1)-colourings lie at finite distance O(n^2). This gives a single mobile four-colour component on Q3; a two-colouring with spare colours witnesses that it exists.
The subcubic n+mu diameter theorem gives 12 for Q3 at every k>=5, and the general k>=Delta+2 threshold gives connectivity.
The broader n+mu conjecture in arXiv:2412.19695 is about diameter, not pointwise eccentricity or the full metric distribution.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Credit the implied mobile-component pattern at k=4 and connectivity and global diameter at k=5. These general results give neither the exact metric of the mobile k=4 component nor that every k=5 state attains the global diameter as an eccentricity.

originality.rationale: Pass for the complete pointwise and pair-distance census, not for basic connectivity or frozen-colouring facts in isolation. In addition to the credited five-colour diameter and frozen example, the four-colour split into isolates plus a unique mobile component is already a consequence of a general recolouring theorem. No inspected statement gives or mechanically determines the simultaneous self-centredness or the full three histograms without a new metric analysis of the finite state graphs.
residual_risks: No full-text inspection of De Meyer's paper; its verified diameter coverage is explicitly credited.
The bounded indexed comparison cannot exclude unpublished or differently indexed finite distance tables.

value.rationale: The smallest cubic hypercube is a natural test case at the sharp frozen-colouring threshold. The same eccentricity at every mobile state across the three different palette regimes is a precise, nontrivial observation beyond the known global diameter. The exhaustive distributions supply a baseline for comparing typical, extremal and pointwise recolouring distances; neither the trivial k=2 row nor rediscovering the k=5 diameter by itself would justify acceptance.
